family_judgments.evidence: Cloze/dialogue allow simple-past passive answers, MCQ forces recognition of the keyed morphology, and transformation additionally requires active-to-passive restructuring.
The transformation foregrounds syntactic voice conversion, whereas the other formats primarily select a fixed passive form; declared KCs remain present but response demands differ materially.
All formats concern the report remaining unprinted when the meeting began.

criteria.evidence: Keyed 'had not been printed' realizes past perfect, negation, and passive BE plus participle.
The response target aligns with the four declared operations.
Solver-proposed 'was not printed' is grammatical and contextually reasonable, while avoiding perfect HAVE.
The printer/copies context and 'before the meeting began' do not force past perfect over simple-past passive.
Reasonable unkeyed 'was not printed' is rejected.
The learner must infer temporal interpretation from a causal printer scenario.
The keyed response contains each declared past-perfect passive-negation component.
No additional response grammar is required.
A learner can reasonably answer 'was not printed' to explain the absence of copies, omitting perfect HAVE.
The dialogue establishes unavailability, not a uniquely required past-perfect form.
The plausible simple-past passive alternative is absent from the accepted responses.
Explanation of an office-printer causal chain adds discourse burden.
B uniquely combines HAD, NOT, BEEN, and PRINTED in the intended passive-perfect structure.
Distractors focus on omissions or malformed alternatives to declared operations.
No listed alternative is both grammatical and an adequate explanation with the target temporal relation.
B is the sole defensible listed option.
Single-choice scoring covers the one defensible option.
The context is straightforward.
Rewriting the active negative past perfect as passive requires passive BE while retaining past perfect and negation.
Passive transformation is part of the declared passive target rather than an unrelated demand.
The source does not provide the passive auxiliary sequence; the learner must construct it.
Equivalent passive wording such as 'The report had not been printed by the time the meeting began' is defensible.
The exact-only key omits reasonable same-meaning passive paraphrases, including 'by the time the meeting began'.
Active-to-passive subject restructuring adds task burden beyond selecting verb morphology.

summary: Rejected: past-perfect form is not determined in cloze/dialogue, their reasonable simple-past passive alternatives are unaccepted, and transformation scoring is too narrow.
